- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct downward quickly.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Tends to overreact to recent volatility, especially when history includes high volatility (e.g., 2023-06-12), leading to over-forecasted peaks.
- Underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 80–82 range) when they follow high prices, suggesting insufficient downward momentum modeling.
- Fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., price dips around mid-month or after policy announcements).
